gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: There was plenty of food left, so the guests ___ have been hungry.
gaps.explanation: The evidence (leftover food) rules out hunger: can't have been.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike — it is the law.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong obligation, often from rules or laws: must wear.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ wear badges at all times inside the plant.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' = a rule that has to be followed.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not have heard the announcement — he had headphones on the whole flight.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have heard' — 'can' supplies the negative deduction before 'not have heard'.
